title: Value Framing Playbook - LLM API Accounts
content:
PURPOSE: One-pager playbook for AE/SDR/SEs to run short, empathy-first positioning conversations vs other LLM API providers. Focus is on converting technical buyers (platform teams, infra, ML engineers) and product-first buyers (startup PMs) who care about latency, cost, and control.

TL;DR MESSAGES:
- We position Redwood on three dimensions: predictable economics, production-ready reliability, and deployment flexibility.
- Top line: "Deliver consistent, low-latency inference where you need it (hosted, dedicated, private) with transparent cost controls and built-in fallbacks."
- Primary proof points: Dedicated GPU pools, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback), token-level observability, and smart routing across model variants.

COMPETITOR SNAPSHOT (short, talk-track friendly):
- OpenAI: strongest degree of model R&D and brand. Strength: newest models, wide community usage. Weakness: less transparent unit economics, fewer private/VPC-first enterprise controls without additional agreements.
- Anthropic: safety-first models and strong alignment work. Strength: philosophic safety posture. Weakness: less mature orchestration for multi-environment serving + fewer cost levers.
- Cohere/Cerence-style vendors: model variety and embedding coverage. Strength: embedding accuracy and specialized models. Weakness: limited dedicated/private deployment story and fewer SRE-grade runbooks.
- Cloud providers (Vertex/Azure OpenAI/Bedrock): strength = consolidation with infra + identity; weakness = lock-in, unpredictable cost per token scaling, and slower model rollouts for open models.
- Self-hosted runtimes (llama.cpp and OSS stacks): strength = cost control at small scale; weakness = operational burden, absent rollouts and SLO guarantees.

FEATURE COMPARISON — how to talk about differences:
(Use short bullet comparisons in conversation; adapt to buyer persona)
- Deployment modes: Redwood = hosted, reserved Dedicated pools, Private (VPC/on-prem) shipped as product. Competitors: often hosted-only or enterprise only via complex contracts. Talk-track: "We give you the same API and rollout model whether it’s in our cloud or your VPC — no rewriting infra."
- Observability & cost breakdowns: Redwood = token-level cost/latency per route, model-level dashboards, trace hooks. Competitors = coarse-grained or absent. Talk-track: "You can see exactly which prompts cost you and optimize without guesswork."
- Reliability/fallbacks: Redwood = policy-based smart routing + automatic fallback to compatible model variants. Competitors = manual re-routing or partial failover. Talk-track: "If your primary model stalls, traffic fails over automatically minimizing tail latency."
- Performance controls: Redwood = batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations by workload. Competitors = limited or developer-implemented. Talk-track: "We tune serving for your workload — not a one-size-fits-all endpoint."
- Compliance & private deployments: Redwood = customer-managed private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, on-prem options. Competitors = partial or slow enterprise offerings. Talk-track: "We’ll run inference in your network under your KMS."
- Pricing & predictability: Redwood = usage for hosted + reserved contracts for Dedicated, clear unit economics. Competitors = opaque or unpredictable egress/compute line items. Talk-track: "Budget forecasts that aren’t guesses — you can buy committed capacity where it matters."

COMMON CUSTOMER TRAPS (what sales will hear) & HOW TO RESPOND
- Trap: "We can self-host and be cheaper."
  Response: Empathize: "Totally — at small scale self-hosting can look cheaper." Then reframe: "Ask how much engineering time you’ll spend keeping latencies stable, implementing rollouts, and building observability. For production SLAs, the ops cost quickly exceeds raw infra cost. We offload that operational risk and provide predictable capacity plans."
- Trap: "We need the latest model from Vendor X — can you match?"
  Response: "We maintain a model catalog and verify performance; where we don’t host the newest proprietary model we provide fast compatibility fallbacks and smart routing so your app stays live while you evaluate."
- Trap: "We’re worried about vendor lock-in."
  Response: "We built the platform to be deployment-agnostic: the same API + rollout semantics run in Hosted, Dedicated, or your VPC. We’ll help you pin model versions and export metrics and cache artifacts if you ever need to migrate."
- Trap: "Pricing is opaque — how much will this cost at scale?"
  Response: "We give token-level cost breakdowns and model recommendations tailored to prompt sets. We also offer Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable unit economics. We can run a short proof-of-concept to model your workload and present a forecast."

REBUTTAL SCRIPTS (short, practice-ready):
- For infra/platform lead who cares about SLOs: "We treat inference like any other critical service — SLOs, canaries, tracing, automatic fallback. Our dedicated pools are architected for predictable p99 latency so you can hit production SLAs."
- For security/compliance buyer: "We support a private control plane and integrate with your KMS/HSM, and provide audit logs and retention controls — we can run a pilot in your VPC so you can validate controls."
- For cost-conscious startup founder: "Start with our hosted catalog and cost observability; once patterns stabilize we can propose a Dedicated commit that lowers per-token costs while guaranteeing throughput."

WIN CONDITIONS (what to get signed off in the meeting)
1) Platform/infra: technical validation — ask for a pilot where we run a representative traffic shape against a dedicated pool.
2) Security: access to a list of required compliance controls + KMS approvals to scope a VPC pilot.
3) Product/PM: delivery of a sample integration and performance/quality report comparing 2 model variants.
4) Procurement: alignment on a 3-month reserved capacity trial or a POC budget to model cost.

SCENARIOS & FIELD PLAY (how to run the call)
- Scenario: Enterprise RFP (long sales cycle)
  Play: Lead with compliance + private deployment story. Ask to see the RFP’s SLO and data residency clauses, propose a staged approach: VPC pilot -> dedicated commit -> enterprise onboarding.
- Scenario: Platform Team evaluating latency variability
  Play: Offer a technical workshop, propose a dedicated pool pilot with p99 targets and set an observability dashboard for both teams.
- Scenario: Startup wants lowest price for embeddings
  Play: Suggest hosted trial with batching/embedding cache enabled, run a 7–14 day cost analysis and propose conversion to Dedicated residual if embeddings volume justifies.

OBJECTION HANDLING FOR COMMON COMPARATORS (quick lines)
- OpenAI: "They lead on model innovation; we lead on inference engineering. If you need the latest novelty, we can integrate or route to those models while giving you the controls and economics to run them in production."
- Cloud provider: "They bundle infra, but you’ll trade off speed of model iteration and transparent per-token economics. We plug into your infra or run privately to avoid long-term lock-in while giving you better inference controls."
- OSS/self-hosting: "OSS gives flexibility, but it’s an engineering tax. For product teams that need uptime and predictable latency, we remove that tax and let you focus on product."

TECHNICAL PROOFS & TALKING POINTS (one-liners you can use)
- "Dedicated GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst capacity keep throughput predictable as traffic ramps."
- "Token-level cost + latency breakdowns let you optimize prompts and measure ROI per feature."
- "Smart routing and automatic fallback keep apps responsive even when a model variant is overloaded."
- "Private control plane + KMS/HSM integrations meet enterprise audit and key management requirements."

QUICK PREP CHECKLIST FOR AEs/SES BEFORE CALL
- Confirm buyer persona and top-3 concerns (latency, cost, compliance).
- Bring a short performance slide: p50/p95/p99 for representative workloads (or offer to run a 48-hour pilot).
- Have an example rollout plan and a proposed committed capacity size if volume is predictable.
- Know the migration story (metrics export, cache artifacts).

LEARNING AGENDA (what to capture during call)
- Current model endpoints in use and their observed p95/p99 latency and cost per 1M tokens.
- Which classification of workloads (real-time chat vs batch embeddings vs reranking).
- Compliance constraints (KMS, data residency, retention).
- Which internal teams own infra cost and who signs procurement.

ATTACHMENTS/ASSETS TO SHARE AFTER CALL
- Short 1-pager: dedicated-pool-poc-template.pdf (pilot scope + acceptance criteria).
- Sample dashboard screenshots for token-level observability.
- Cost-forecast workbook (we’ll run offline and return estimates).

NOTES & TODOS (internal)
- Follow up: run 48-hour representative workload with smart routing enabled and share p99 improvement metric.
- Create a short demo repo showing how to pin model versions and export metrics to Prometheus/Grafana.
- Draft a short procurement-friendly one-pager explaining Dedicated commit options and cancellation terms.

ENDNOTE: Keep conversations tightly tied to the buyer’s primary pain (latency unpredictability, hidden unit economics, operational risk). Use the platform differentiation (same API across deployments, token-level observability, reserved capacity) to move the buyer from curiosity to a low-friction pilot.

-- Maya (author)
